binders: m is an arbitrary natural number.
Omega is an arbitrary finite type, serving as the sample space.

run is an enhanced certified m-step recursive-summation run over Omega. Its data include a finite probability mass function P, positive natural parameters p and r, coefficients a_0,...,a_m, error families delta_k and beta_k for k=0,...,m-1, and a function T : Real -> Real.
lambda is an arbitrary real number.
hypotheses: The probability weights satisfy P(omega)>=0 for every omega and sum_omega P(omega)=1.
The parameters satisfy p>0 and r>0.
Let u_q=(1/2)^(q-1), with natural subtraction in the exponent. For every k and omega, |delta_k(omega)|<=u_p and 1+delta_k(omega)>=0.

Define c_0(omega)=a_0, x_k(omega)=c_k(omega)+a_(k+1), and c_(k+1)(omega)=x_k(omega)(1+delta_k(omega)). Then T(x_k(omega))=x_k(omega)(1+beta_k(omega)); moreover, x_k(omega)=0 implies delta_k(omega)=0 and beta_k(omega)=0.
For each k, beta_k depends only on delta_j with j<k. For every real-valued X depending only on those earlier delta values, E_P[X delta_k]=E_P[X beta_k].
Define epsilon_k=delta_k-beta_k. Then |epsilon_k(omega)|<=u_p for every k and omega.
For each k and every real-valued X depending only on epsilon_j with j<k, E_P[X epsilon_k]=0.

For an error vector e, define Phi_0(e)=product from k=0 to m-1 of (1+e_k), and Phi_(j+1)(e)=product from k=j to m-1 of (1+e_k). For all i,j in {0,...,m}, 0<=E_P[(Phi_i(epsilon)-1)(Phi_j(epsilon)-1)]<=gamma_m(u_p^2), where gamma_m(t)=(1+t)^m-1.
For every i in {0,...,m} and omega, |Phi_i(delta)(omega)-Phi_i(epsilon)(omega)|<=gamma_m(u_p+u_(p+r))-gamma_m(u_p).
The exact sum S=sum from i=0 to m of a_i is nonzero.
conclusions: The P-probability of the event |c_m(omega)-S|/|S| <= kappa(a) [sqrt(gamma_m(u_p^2)/lambda) + gamma_m(u_p+u_(p+r)) - gamma_m(u_p)] is at least 1-lambda, where kappa(a)=(sum from i=0 to m of |a_i|)/|S|.
mathematical_definitions: S=sum from i=0 to m of a_i is the exact sum.
The computed sum is hat S(omega)=c_m(omega), where c_0(omega)=a_0 and c_(k+1)(omega)=(c_k(omega)+a_(k+1))(1+delta_k(omega)).
E_P[X]=sum over omega in Omega of P(omega)X(omega), and Pr_P(E)=sum over omega satisfying E of P(omega).
u_q=(1/2)^(q-1), where q-1 is truncated natural subtraction; because p>0, u_p=2^(1-p) in the usual integer-exponent notation.
kappa(a)=(sum_i |a_i|)/|sum_i a_i| is the absolute l1 condition number of summation.
No norm other than real absolute value and the induced coefficient l1 sum occurs.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite discrete certified recursive-summation run satisfying the stated bounded-error, adaptedness, centering, covariance, and multiplicative-discrepancy conditions, and for every confidence parameter lambda strictly between 0 and 1, if the exact coefficient sum is nonzero, then with probability at least 1-lambda the relative error of the recursively perturbed sum is at most the summation condition number times sqrt(gamma_m(u_p^2)/lambda) plus the correction gamma_m(u_p+u_(p+r))-gamma_m(u_p).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result applies only to finite sample spaces and finite discrete probability distributions.
Although Omega is only declared finite, existence of a run includes weights summing to 1, so Omega must in fact be nonempty whenever such a run exists.
The universal statement is vacuous if no enhanced certified run with the required embedded data and proofs exists.
The implication is vacuous when S=0 or when lambda is not strictly between 0 and 1; the asserted conclusion is only reached under S!=0 and 0<lambda<1.
The case m=0 is allowed. Then there are no error indices, the computed sum equals a_0, and all relevant products are empty products.
No independence or identical-distribution assumption is encoded. Only the explicitly stated adapted moment equalities, covariance bounds, and pointwise bounds are available.
Adaptedness is encoded extensionally as dependence only on earlier error coordinates; no sigma-algebra or general conditional expectation is present.
The function T is otherwise arbitrary and is constrained only at the specified pre-update values x_k.
No concrete floating-point format, rounding mode, representability condition, overflow, underflow, or implementation semantics is encoded.
The multiplier convention has Phi_0(e)=Phi_1(e)=product from k=0 to m-1 of (1+e_k) when m>0; this duplication is exactly what the supplied definition encodes.
Real division is formally total, but the target explicitly ensures S!=0 and lambda>0 for the two denominators used in the conclusion.
